name: Fold a Paper Airplane
description: Fold a classic dart paper airplane that flies straight and far. No tools needed — just a single sheet of paper.
components: 1x Sheet of A4 or letter-size paper

steps.instruction: Place the paper in portrait orientation (tall, not wide). Fold it in half lengthwise by bringing the left edge to meet the right edge. Crease firmly, then unfold.
steps.visual_cue: The paper is flat with a single vertical crease running top to bottom down the exact center. The paper should be in portrait orientation (taller than wide).
during_action_cues: User picks up the paper or lays it flat — check orientation: should be portrait (tall), not landscape (wide)
User's hands move to fold — watch the direction: they should bring the LEFT edge toward the RIGHT edge (or vice versa), creating a vertical fold
The fold line should run top-to-bottom, NOT left-to-right
After folding, user should press/crease along the fold firmly with fingers or a flat edge
User should then unfold the paper back flat — the crease should remain visible
common_errors: Paper is in landscape orientation (wide, not tall) — CATCH THIS BEFORE THEY FOLD
Folding horizontally (top edge to bottom edge) instead of vertically (left to right) — this is the most common mistake
Not creasing firmly enough — the center line should be clearly visible after unfolding
Forgetting to unfold — the paper should be flat with a visible crease, not still folded

steps.instruction: Fold the top-left corner down so its edge aligns with the center crease. Then do the same with the top-right corner. Both corners fold down to meet at the center.
steps.visual_cue: Two diagonal folds form a triangle/arrow point at the top of the paper. The folded edges of both corners meet precisely along the center crease. The bottom half remains a flat rectangle.
during_action_cues: User reaches for a top corner — watch WHICH corner and WHERE they fold it toward
The corner should fold DOWN and INWARD toward the center crease line
The diagonal edge of the fold should align with the vertical center crease
Watch that the fold is tight against the center line — no gap between the folded edge and the crease
After one corner, watch them do the same with the other corner — both should be symmetrical
The point at the top where both corners meet should be sharp, not rounded or offset
common_errors: Folding only one corner and forgetting the other — remind them to do both sides
Corner doesn't reach the center crease — there's a visible gap between the folded edge and the center line
Corner goes PAST the center crease, overlapping — the folded edge should land exactly ON the center line
Corners are folded at different angles, making the point asymmetrical — one side is wider than the other
Folding the bottom corners instead of the top corners

steps.instruction: Fold the triangular point down so the tip reaches about 2-3 cm (roughly 1 inch) above the bottom edge of the paper. Crease well.
steps.visual_cue: The triangle has been folded down like an envelope flap. The tip of the triangle points downward but stops about a finger-width above the bottom edge. The overall shape looks like a wide envelope or a house shape.
during_action_cues: User grabs the pointed top — watch which direction they fold it: should be DOWNWARD (toward the bottom of the paper)
The point should fold DOWN over the diagonal edges, lying flat against the paper
Watch how FAR down they fold it — the tip should NOT touch the very bottom edge; it stops about 2-3 cm (one finger-width) above it
The fold line should be roughly horizontal, running straight across the paper
User should crease this fold firmly
common_errors: Folding the point UPWARD instead of downward — the point must fold toward the bottom of the paper
Folding the point all the way to the bottom edge — it should stop about 2-3 cm short, leaving a small rectangle of paper visible below the tip
Not folding enough — the point should come most of the way down, leaving only about a finger-width gap
The fold line is crooked/diagonal instead of straight across — this will cause asymmetry later

steps.instruction: Fold the new top-left corner down to the center crease, then the top-right corner. These are similar to step 2 but start higher up since the triangle is folded down. The new corner folds should meet at the center just above the folded-down triangle tip.
steps.visual_cue: Two new diagonal folds create a sharper, narrower point at the top. Below the new folds, the small triangle tip from step 3 peeks out — a small triangular tab is visible where the new corners meet.
during_action_cues: User reaches for the new top corners — these are above the horizontal fold from step 3
Each corner folds DOWN and INWARD to the center crease, same motion as step 2
Watch that the folded edges align with the center crease — no gaps, no overlaps
The point where both new corners meet should be just ABOVE the tip of the folded-down triangle from step 3
A small triangular tab from step 3 should be visible poking out below the new corner folds — this is important for the next step
Both sides should be symmetrical
common_errors: New folds don't reach the center crease — visible gap between folded edge and center
Folding over the triangle flap from step 3 — the flap should still be visible underneath
The new folds start from the wrong spot — they should start from the top edge of the paper, above the step 3 horizontal fold
Asymmetrical folds — one side is wider or at a different angle than the other

steps.instruction: See that small triangle tip poking out from under the corner folds? Fold it UPWARD over the two corner flaps to lock them in place. It acts like a tab holding an envelope closed.
steps.visual_cue: The small triangular tab is now folded UP and over the two corner flaps, pinning them down. It looks like the clasp on an envelope. All the folds on this side should feel locked and secure.
during_action_cues: User should identify the small triangle tab peeking out below the corner folds from step 4
They fold this tab UPWARD (toward the top of the paper), flipping it over the edges of the two corner folds
The tab should lay flat over the corner folds, locking them in place
Watch that they fold the RIGHT flap — it's the small triangle from step 3, not one of the corner folds
common_errors: Skipping this step entirely — remind them this locking fold is important for structural integrity
Folding the wrong flap — they should fold the small triangle from step 3, not undo a corner fold
Folding the tab DOWNWARD instead of upward — it needs to go UP and over the corner folds to lock them
Not pressing the tab flat — it should be creased firmly so it stays in place

steps.instruction: Flip the entire paper over (face down). Fold it in half along the center crease so the folded side is on the outside. Then fold each wing down — the wing's bottom edge should line up with the bottom fold of the body. Your airplane is done!
steps.visual_cue: A completed dart airplane: pointed nose, two symmetrical wings angled slightly upward from the body, a flat narrow body along the bottom. Viewed from the front, it forms a Y-shape. Viewed from the side, the wing edge is parallel to the body.
during_action_cues: First: user should FLIP the paper over — all the folds from previous steps are now face-down on the table
Then: user folds the paper in half along the existing center crease — the folded/layered side should be on the OUTSIDE
After folding in half, the shape should be a long triangle with the point on one side
Then: user folds one wing down — the fold should start at the nose and run to the tail, with the wing edge aligning with the bottom body fold
Then: flip and fold the other wing to match — both wings should be the same width and angle
Wings should angle slightly upward from the body when held level — not straight out flat, not drooping down
common_errors: Forgetting to flip the paper over first — the clean side should face up when folding in half
Folding in half the wrong way — the fold should be along the existing center crease
Wings are asymmetrical — one wider or at a different angle than the other
Wings fold too far down — the wing edge should align with the bottom body fold, not extend past it
Wings droop downward instead of angling slightly up — they should hold a slight upward angle (dihedral)
